ai.title: Refactor admin, API, and prompt functions to accept logger
ai.summary: Backend functions including gradeRun, relabelForUserHandler, fastRewrite, and requestRelevantFiles now accept a logger instance via their params object. This replaces global logger imports and positional arguments with explicit dependency injection for better traceability. Scope covers backend admin tools, API handlers, and LLM prompt generation files. The change standardizes logger usage across the backend, ensuring log context matches the active request or session.

eli5.text: The backend team updated several behind-the-scenes functions so they now receive a logging tool through their parameters instead of fetching a global logger. This lets each request or session carry its own tracing context, making logs easier to follow. Nothing changes for you as a user right now; this is internal housekeeping to improve debugging and traceability.

ai.title: Add git clone retry logic to evals setup-test-repo
ai.summary: Added executeGitCommandWithRetry helper in evals/git-evals/setup-test-repo.ts to wrap git clone, fetch, and checkout calls with exponential backoff (max 3 retries, 1s base delay). Clone timeout raised from 120s to 600s; added GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT=1000 and GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME=30 env vars to both CI and local paths. Local path now also runs fetch origin commitSha with --quiet, matching CI behavior. Internal evals only; no user-facing surface affected.

eli5.text: When the automated test system tries to download a project's code from its online storage location, it now automatically retries a few times with short pauses in between if the download fails, instead of giving up immediately. The system also gives downloads up to ten minutes to complete (previously two) and is more tolerant of slow network connections. This makes the test setup process more reliable behind the scenes; you may not notice it unless a download was previously failing, in which case it is more likely to succeed on its own now. Effective 2025-10-09, this affects only the internal evaluation tooling and has no impact on any live features or user-facing functionality.

ai.title: Introduce AgentRuntimeDeps for dependency injection
ai.summary: Refactors backend agent execution to use explicit dependency injection via new `AgentRuntimeDeps` type. Replaces direct imports of `startAgentRun` and `logger` in tool handlers and core steps with injected dependencies passed through `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` and `runAgentStep`. Updates `main-prompt.ts`, `run-agent-step.ts`, `run-programmatic-step.ts`, and `spawn-agent-inline.ts` to accept these deps, decoupling runtime logic from specific implementations.

eli5.text: The backend now wires up its helper tools (like logging and run tracking) by handing each step an explicit bundle of dependencies, rather than having each step reach out and grab them directly. What you experience: the agent flow keeps working the same way today, but the internal plumbing is decoupled so steps receive what they need through shared context instead of hardcoding imports. This is live now and is purely a refactor - no new visible behavior, just cleaner connections behind the scenes.

eli5.text: When an assistant run finishes, the system can now explicitly close it out instead of just opening it. This pairs with the existing start step so runs have both a beginning and an end recorded. If you looked, you'd see the change across five implementation files plus the shared type definition, each adding the matching finish call. The change is in place today.

ai.title: Add addAgentStep to AgentRuntimeDeps
ai.summary: The `AgentRuntimeDeps` interface in `packages/types` now requires an `addAgentStep` function. Implementations in backend, testing, and evals were updated to provide this dependency, shifting step recording from direct imports to dependency injection. This ensures `run-agent-step.ts` receives `addAgentStep` via the `loopAgentSteps` parameters rather than importing it statically.

eli5.text: When the assistant agent takes a turn doing its work, that turn is now logged through a shared service channel instead of each part of the system fetching the logging tool directly on its own. This means the backend, the test environments, and the evaluation tools all now wire in a logging function the same way, so every part of the system follows one consistent path when recording what the assistant did. It is the same kind of tidy-up that earlier made the same logging function required elsewhere, and it is live now: any existing flows that record agent steps behave the same for you, they just do it through the new shared channel. Nothing about what you actually experience changes here, this is behind-the-scenes housekeeping so the system stays consistent and easier to maintain.

eli5.text: The main helper that runs your coding tasks has been broken into a team of more specialized helpers, each focused on a narrower job like searching code, listing folders, or sketching out new code before it is written. What you experience is that planning, reviewing, and thinking steps now route through these dedicated roles instead of one general one, and one old helper named Buffy the Orchestrator coordinates them. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping with no direct change to any app or command you run today.

eli5.text: The codebuff assistant had a bunch of shared definitions (like logging formats and data types) living in a separate package called @codebuff/types. That package has been deleted, and everyone who needed those definitions now imports them directly from the @codebuff/common package instead. If you peek at the project structure, the scattered helper files under the old package location are gone, and the corresponding files inside the common package now hold all of these shared definitions in one place. The end user sees no difference in how the assistant behaves today, but the codebase is now tidier and easier for the team to maintain.

ai.title: Evals run from git worktree snapshot
ai.summary: run-eval-set.ts creates a git worktree per run via createEvalWorktree(), freezing code at current HEAD. run-git-evals.ts accepts worktreePath, resolving run-single-eval-process.ts inside it. Temp eval-commit file path switched to path.resolve for worktree compatibility. cleanupEvalWorktree() removes worktree on exit, falling back to git worktree prune.

eli5.text: When the team runs its automated evaluations of the agent these days, the tooling first clones a frozen copy of the entire code base into a temporary folder before doing anything else. That snapshot is taken at the exact commit the evaluator is testing, so local experiments and CI runs are judged against the same fixed body of code instead of whatever might be sitting in your working directory. The cloned copy is deleted automatically when the run finishes, and if that cleanup somehow fails the code tells git to prune it away as a backup. You wouldn't see this if you're just chatting with the agent. It only changes how the engineering team measures whether a given version of the agent behaves correctly.

ai.title: Revert AI SDK dependency injection in agent runtime
ai.summary: Removed `promptAiSdkStream` from `AgentRuntimeDeps` interface and implementations. `backend/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts` and `common/src/types/contracts/agent-runtime.ts` no longer export or require the LLM stream function. `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts` now imports `promptAiSdkStream` directly from `./llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk`. Type definitions for `StreamChunk` moved to `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. `promptAiSdkStream` signature updated to explicit params instead of `ParamsOf<PromptAiSdkStreamFn>`.

eli5.text: The team took a piece of wiring that connected the agent's brain (the reasoning engine) to the rest of the system and moved it from a plug-in slot to a direct connection. Instead of telling every part of the system to bring its own copy of the brain module, each part now simply asks for what it needs at the moment it needs it. This means the agent's ability to stream replies is now handled through one consistent path rather than being passed around as a dependency, making the wiring simpler and the flow of requests more predictable. You wouldn't see a visual difference, but the system is less likely to get tangled or confused about which brain module is in use.
